formal_object.rationale: Group losses are source-declared training means and gamma>0 defines a static entropic maximum.

operations_and_conditions.rationale: C02: F=max_a sum a_g L_g+gamma H(a). Condition: gamma>0 and simplex weights B02: a_g=softmax(L_g/gamma), gradient=sum a_g grad L_g. Condition: All groups nonempty

derivation.rationale: The normalized Gibbs optimum and max-to-max+gamma log G bounds follow the finite simplex entropy dual; differentiation includes loss dependence.

assumptions.rationale: Groups are declared by training provenance, not test outcomes; each has positive sample count. All group losses use the same units and fixed gamma. Smooth worst-training-group loss is not worst-test-task generalization. Finite gradient descent with ridge is an approximate optimization, not Sagawa's persistent online group adversary. These are conditional premises, not observed benchmark facts.

method_expression.rationale: Explicit smooth-max gradient with finite iterations is a valid conditional construction. It is not the author persistent online adversary.

prediction_and_falsifier.rationale: Benefits, if any, should track changes in observed group loss dispersion and transfer to predeclared test tasks; small gamma increases emphasis on the current hard training group. Falsification: Matched ERM or the author online group-DRO achieves equal or better full-task tradeoff; lowering training F alone cannot establish transfer.

closest_alternative.rationale: The source-inspected Sagawa objective/update and ERM are distinct mandatory alternatives; training-source worst risk is not native worst-task generalization. This check only reviews the stated mathematical comparison; exhaustive full-text/author-code/native collision and originality decisions remain pending.
